argument_summary: The admissible record supports only a narrow defense of certification: the release clears aggregate launch readiness by 2.3 percentage points, had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and is supported by general model-card and AI risk-management principles that allow documented limitations, measurement, and ongoing monitoring. That is enough to argue the launch is operationally supportable on a weak, caveated basis. It is not enough to claim the materiality question is resolved. The strongest accurate packet is therefore limited certification support with an explicit caveat that the mortgage servicing assistant segment remains below target, is named in two servicer pilot commitments, and remains subject to unresolved legal and policy interpretation.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to resolve the audit question. The relevant point is that the record already supports a bounded, caveated treatment without overstating compliance.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not allow us to claim clean satisfaction of the disclosure predicate on this record. Admissible evidence shows a named launch use case with a 1.1 percentage point gap, two pilot commitments, an open legal review, and no evidence in the packet of resolution, disclosure, or approved risk acceptance. The defensible position is narrower: aggregate readiness evidence can support certification readiness in a practical sense, but policy compliance should be characterized as caveated rather than complete unless and until one of the stated policy off-ramps is shown.
concessions: The admissible record does not show that the limitation was resolved before launch.
The admissible record does not show that the limitation was disclosed as required.
The admissible record does not show an approved risk-acceptance record for this named launch use case.
The 5% projected traffic characterization does not by itself resolve materiality because the affected segment is named in pilot commitments and legal review is still open.
Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance support documentation and monitoring, but do not by themselves prove that an unresolved disclosure predicate has been satisfied.
